decomposition.assumptions_disclosed: X ~ Poisson and collisions mutually independent; the stability ladder supports the absence of long-range correlation (flat in 16..1024 periods, W 1..64, R 256..65536) but does not prove independence at 2^87.67 periods. This is a rho-heuristic CONJECTURE, and the bound charged is the smaller of the analytic value and the measured carrier CP-95 lower bound.

returns.source: returns_v20.json: per-TRAIL exact tracking on the declared walk, 38,400 trails, 0 exact (S,t) returns, 0 identity restarts, positive control detects 1.04e6 S returns at q=1031
returns.structural_argument: the row index is prod = (S XOR (t*2654435761 mod 2^64) XOR trail*7919) mod R, so the next state is a function of (S, t) and t increases strictly inside a trail; the pair (S, t) never recurs, therefore a walker's future never repeats and the classical rho-cycle death does not exist on this walk
returns.v19_error: v19 divided a per-walker probability by 2^20 and claimed 5.845e-09; that division is wrong (each dead walker loses its own work, so the loss fraction is the per-trail rate) and the underlying zero was measured on coefficient pairs, not states

carrier.label: X_R256_W64_p16
carrier.why_carrier: production success comes from collisions between DISTINCT walkers (per-trail load 2^-40.66); at W=64 only 1.6% of collisions are within-walker, and the bound counts ONLY cross-walker relations, so it is the mix-matched statistic

transfer.not_claimed: that a 37-53 bit fixture group is the P-256 subgroup; the fixture is a stand-in at matched load lambda = 0.634
transfer.statement: success per challenge is measured on the production selector, cross-walker only, and is FLAT in coverage (16..1024 periods), in walker count (1..64) and in R (256..65536) wherever the exact CP intervals overlap; the remaining step to 2^87.67 periods is DISCLOSED AS A CONJECTURE (a rho-style heuristic: the per-period row hazard has no measured dependence on the period count), not as a measurement, and the bound charged is the carrier cell's own CP-95 lower bound, not an extrapolated point
